tip: Baswn i'n means I would. The 'n links Baswn i to the verb: Baswn i'n plannu = I would plant.
Basai is the he or it would form; Baswn is I would. Basai fe'n costio = it would cost.
For reported would, use y byddai (that he would): Addawodd e y byddai'n dod = he promised he would come.
Front the doer for emphasis: Ni oedd wedi paratoi = it was us who prepared, literally we were who prepared.
Taswn i means if I were, the informal conditional: Taswn i yn dy le di = if I were in your place.
lle joins a place to what happened there, like where: yr ysgol lle dysgodd hi = the school where she learned.
taw marks a reported emphasis in south Welsh, like that it was: Dwedodd hi taw hi = she said it was her.
beidio â means not to; after â the next word takes an aspirate mutation, so poeni becomes phoeni in beidio â phoeni.
a opens an indirect yes or no question, like whether: Gofynnodd... a oedd = asked whether it was.
cyn i means before; the verb after softens, so dod becomes ddod: cyn i'r gaeaf ddod = before winter comes.
Pe na bai means if it weren't; pe sets an unreal condition and na makes it negative: Pe na bai'n bwrw glaw.
Add -af for most or -est: poeth (hot) becomes poetha, hottest: y diwrnod poetha'r flwyddyn = the hottest day.
A opens a yes or no question and softens the next word: byddai becomes fyddai in A fyddai'n bosib = would it be possible.
dy (your) softens the next consonant: car becomes gar and beic becomes feic in dy gar a dy feic.
